description: Config for the standalone Renovate run in .github/workflows/renovate.yml. Automerge is enabled because the PHP base image is now pinned to an explicit release and needs automated bumps. No 'schedule' here on purpose: run timing is owned solely by the workflow cron, so this config never blocks an on-demand workflow_dispatch run. 'platformAutomerge' is off because GitHub's auto-merge queue only releases a PR once required checks pass, which would need branch protection; instead the workflow dispatches .github/workflows/validate-build.yml on each renovate/* branch (a bot push starts no workflow run, an explicit dispatch does) and Renovate merges once that check is green - usually on the following run. 'prHourlyLimit' is switched off from its default of 2: that default counts every PR opened in the current clock hour, including ones already closed (for example the per-dependency PRs pruned when this config moved to a single group), and once it is reached Renovate still creates the branch but silently skips the PR - a debug-level event, so an info-level run shows 'Branch created' and nothing else and the workflow's log assertions still pass. One grouped PR per run needs no rate limiting. Note: 'comment' is not a Renovate option and would abort the entire run with a config-validation error, so annotations must live in this 'description' field.

kubernetes.description: The chart's telemetry sidecar images are pinned inside charts/bedrock-website/templates/deployment.yaml, and the kubernetes manager ships with no default file pattern, so those files are invisible to Renovate until they are listed here. Helm templating is not a problem: the manager reads 'image:' lines with a strict Docker reference regex line by line, and the YAML parse it uses for apiVersion updates fails closed (a debug message, no error) on the '{{ ... }}' placeholders.

packageRules.description: Everything actionable lands in one branch/PR, so a run produces a single validate-build.yml dispatch and a single merge rather than one per dependency. The managers are listed explicitly instead of grouping '*': github-actions must stay out of the group because GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push under .github/workflows, and a grouped branch containing such a change would fail for every other update in it too. Combined with the top-level 'separateMajorMinor: false', which stops Renovate splitting major updates into their own branch, this yields exactly one renovate/* branch per run.
Bump the pinned PHP base image in the Dockerfile. A merged bump is published by the next image_build.yml run as a new immutable calendar version, which is what deployments then move to.

This repository's own image, rendered from the chart's appVersion. It is calendar-versioned rather than semver and its rollout is a deliberate, by-hand Chart.yaml edit (docs/image-versioning.md), so Renovate must not track it. Disabling it by name is what makes that stick: the '# renovate:ignore' comment convention is not honoured by the kubernetes manager, which would instead read the templated tag as no tag at all.

A sidecar image bump edits a chart template, so the chart version has to move with it - the Kustomize overlays inflate the chart from this repository and nothing else would signal that the rendered manifests changed. 'bumpVersions' does that inside the same commit. The matchString starts at a newline because Renovate compiles it without the multiline flag, so '^version:' would only match the beginning of Chart.yaml rather than its version line.

GitHub Actions updates are listed on the dependency dashboard instead of raising branches: GITHUB_TOKEN has no 'workflow' scope, so pushing a change under .github/workflows is rejected and the run would fail on every attempt. Tick an item on the dashboard only if you intend to apply that bump by hand.

bedrock/composer.json is deliberately unmanaged. Its requirements are open '>0' constraints with no committed composer.lock, so the image resolves current plugin releases through 'composer update' on every build - the weekly rebuild already picks them up and the calendar version makes that visible. Renovate has nothing to pin here and would only raise no-op noise.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Disabled because the run authenticates with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, which cannot read Dependabot alerts: that is a GitHub App 'vulnerability_alerts' permission and there is no matching key for the Actions token's 'permissions:' block, so it cannot be granted from the workflow. Leaving this enabled only produced 'WARN: Cannot access vulnerability alerts' on every run (a warning, so the log check still passed) and never any extra PR. Nothing is lost in practice either: Dependabot alerts do not cover the pinned Docker base image, and the github-actions manager is already dashboard-only. Re-enable this together with a PAT that has the 'security_events' scope if alert-driven PRs are ever wanted.
